scheme1_name: CBSE Merit Scholarship Scheme for Single Girl Child (SGC)

comparisons.scheme1_value: Financial aid for meritorious single girl students to continue secondary education (classes 11-12).
comparisons.scheme2_value: Micro-credit financing for individuals and small businesses to start or expand income-generating enterprises.

comparisons.scheme1_value: Single girl children only; must be studying in CBSE-affiliated schools, classes 11-12.
comparisons.scheme2_value: Any individual, proprietor, partnership, or company running a non-farm micro business (e.g., shop, service, manufacturing, allied-agriculture).

comparisons.scheme1_value: Rs. 1,000 per month for up to 24 months (Rs. 24,000 total over 2 years).
comparisons.scheme2_value: Loans up to Rs. 20 lakh depending on category: Shishu (up to Rs. 50,000), Kishore (up to Rs. 5 lakh), Tarun (up to Rs. 10 lakh), Tarun Plus (up to Rs. 20 lakh).

comparisons.scheme1_value: Grant (free money, not a loan); disbursed monthly via bank transfer.
comparisons.scheme2_value: Loan (must be repaid with interest); interest rates set by lending institutions per RBI guidelines.

comparisons.scheme1_value: Must have scored 70% or more in CBSE class 10 examination.
comparisons.scheme2_value: No academic requirement; applicant should have skills/experience relevant to the proposed business activity.

comparisons.scheme1_value: Gross family income must not exceed Rs. 8,00,000 per annum.
comparisons.scheme2_value: No income cap mentioned; applicant must have satisfactory credit record and not be a defaulter to any bank or financial institution.

comparisons.scheme1_value: Must be an Indian national; single girl child (including twins); tuition fee cap: Rs. 2,500/month in class 10, Rs. 3,000/month in classes 11-12 (NRI: Rs. 6,000/month); regular attendance and good conduct required.
comparisons.scheme2_value: Individual borrowers or legal entities; must not be a defaulter; no negative credit history.

comparisons.scheme1_value: Aadhaar card + passport-size photograph + student ID card.
comparisons.scheme2_value: One of: Voter ID, Driving Licence, PAN, Aadhaar, Passport, or Government-issued photo ID (self-attested).

comparisons.scheme1_value: Income affidavit on Rs. 50 stamp paper (self-declaration), attested by Gazetted Officer/SDM/First-Class Magistrate.
comparisons.scheme2_value: For Shishu: none. For Kishore/Tarun/Tarun Plus: 6 months' bank statements, last 2 years' balance sheets + income tax/sales tax returns (if loan ≥ Rs. 2 lakh), projected balance sheet.

comparisons.scheme1_value: Class 10 mark sheet (class 11 mark sheet for renewals); admission proof; fee receipt verified by school principal.
comparisons.scheme2_value: For Shishu: quotation of machinery/items, business licences/registration. For Kishore/Tarun/Tarun Plus: project report with technical & economic viability, Partnership Deed/Memorandum & Articles (if applicable).

comparisons.scheme1_value: Online via CBSE scholarship portal (cbse.gov.in/cbsenew/scholar.html); requires school verification; renewal requires courier of signed confirmation to CBSE headquarters.
comparisons.scheme2_value: Online via Udyamimitra portal (udyamimitra.in) or Jan Samarth, or directly at bank branches.

comparisons.scheme1_value: Register → Enter class 10 roll number & DOB → Fill undertaking & affidavit → Scan & upload → Print confirmation (renew: courier to CBSE).
comparisons.scheme2_value: Visit portal → Register with email/mobile → Select category (Shishu/Kishore/Tarun) → Fill business details → Attach documents → Submit & note Application Number.

comparisons.scheme1_value: Annual windows notified yearly on CBSE scholarship page; specific dates vary by session.
Scholarship renewed yearly if conditions (attendance, marks, conduct) are met; disbursed via ECS/NEFT monthly.
comparisons.scheme2_value: Loan approval and disbursement depend on lender; varies by lending institution and loan category.

comparisons.scheme1_value: Tuition fee cap is strict: exceeding Rs. 2,500/month (class 10) or Rs. 3,000/month (classes 11-12) makes applicant ineligible.
comparisons.scheme2_value: No agents or middlemen exist for MUDRA loans; anyone claiming to facilitate for a fee is fraudulent.

comparisons.scheme1_value: Family income must be proven by attested affidavit; no exceptions to Rs. 8 lakh annual income cap.
comparisons.scheme2_value: Defaulters to any bank or financial institution are ineligible; credit history must be satisfactory.

recommendation:
**These are two completely different schemes for different life stages:**

**Choose CBSE SGC Scholarship if:** You are a single girl child studying in classes 11-12 in a CBSE school, scored 70%+ in class 10, and your family income is below Rs. 8 lakh/year. This gives you FREE financial aid (Rs. 1,000/month) to support your education.

**Choose MUDRA Yojana if:** You are an adult wanting to start or grow a small business (shop, service, manufacturing, etc.) and need a loan (which you must repay with interest) up to Rs. 20 lakh. This is for self-employment, not education.

**Key Difference:** CBSE SGC is a **grant (free money)** for girl students' education; MUDRA is a **loan (borrowed money)** for entrepreneurs to build businesses.

⚠️ **Disclaimer:** This is AI guidance based on official context provided. For final decisions, verify with official sources: CBSE (cbse.gov.in) for scholarships or MUDRA (mudra.org.in) for loans. This is not legal or financial advice.
